title_clean: The Shorter Series of Questions and Answers — Cūḷavedalla Sutta (MN 44)
description_short: Bhante Bodhidhamma explores the profound dialogue between Dhammadinnā and Visākha on identity, the Eightfold Path, and formations.
description_long:
In this enlightening teaching, Bhante Bodhidhamma examines the Cūḷavedalla Sutta (MN 44), featuring the remarkable dialogue between the nun Dhammadinnā—named by the Buddha as foremost in teaching—and her former husband Visākha. The talk begins with clarification of key terminology, particularly exploring sakkāyadiṭṭhi (identity-view or personhood) and its relationship to the five khandhas.

Bhante Bodhidhamma guides us through Dhammadinnā's systematic explanations of fundamental Buddhist concepts: the nature of identity and its clinging to the psychophysical organism, the origin and cessation of this attachment through taṇhā (craving), and the twenty forms of personality-view based on the five aggregates. The discussion moves through the three aggregates of the Noble Eightfold Path—sīla (ethics), samādhi (concentration), and paññā (wisdom)—before exploring the nature of concentration (ekaggatā) and its foundations in the four satipaṭṭhānas.

The talk concludes with an examination of the three types of saṅkhāra (volitional formations): bodily, verbal, and mental, offering practical insights into how our habits and intentions manifest through body, speech, and mind. This teaching provides both newcomers and experienced practitioners with profound understanding of core Buddhist psychology and the path to liberation.
